problem: Bound on the size of Permutation Set for Isomorphism
proof_numbered:
0001 | $\textbf{Claim :}$ $G, H $  are  partitioned into sub-graphs             $\{ G_1,G_2 \cdots G_x \}$ and  $\{ H_1,H_2 \cdots H_x \} $  . For each $G_i$ we constructed a set permutation, $\beta_i$ such that $ \exists \pi \in \beta_i, G_i^{\pi} \simeq H_i$.$\pi$ is a part of $P$ such that $G^P=H$. Each $\beta_i$ has maximum  $ \beta $ permutations. Isomorphism test of  $G,H$ can be done determined in    $O((x \times \beta)^c)$ time where $c$ is a constant provided that $P$ exists as described as above .
0002 | 
0003 | 
0004 | 
0005 | $\textbf{Proof:}$
0006 | 
0007 | 
0008 |   An algorithmic proof  is presented here.
0009 |  The computational complexity of of finding $P$ is polynomial in $\beta$.  
0010 | 
0011 | 
0012 | We construct the generating set of automorphism group of $H$ using  $\beta_k$, for all $k$. As we know, constructing  generating set of automorphism group of  $H$ is a  GI complete problem **[1]**. So, we try to construct the generating set of $Aut(H)$ . The technique used in the paper **[2]**  by E. Luks can used here. 
0013 | 
0014 | 
0015 | **Notation:**
0016 | 
0017 | From now on, $G, H$ are adjacency matrices of graphs $G, H$ respectively. $H_k, G_k$ are blocks or sub-matrices of matrix $H, G$ respectively. The adjacency matrix of graph $H_k \cup  H_e$ is $M_{(k,e)}$ where   $M_{(k,e)} =\left( \begin{array}{ccc} H_e & R_{k,e} \\ R_{k,e}^{T} & H_k\\ \end{array} \right) $,  where, $R_{k,e}$ is the non symmetric sub-matrix of adjacency matrix $H$.  Here, $R_{k,e}$ represents  edges  between $H_k,  H_e$.  Similarly,  $S_{k,e}$ represents  edges  between $G_k, G_e$.
0018 | $$H = \begin{bmatrix}
0019 | H_{(x)} & R_{(x, x-1)} & R_{(x,x-2)} & \dots & \dots & R_{(x,1)} \\
0020 | R_{(x,x-1)} & H_{(x-1)} & R_{(x-1,x-2)} & \dots & \dots & R_{(x-1,1)} \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \ddots & \vdots \\
0021 | R_{(x,1)} & R_{(x-1,1)} & R_{(x-2,1)} & \dots & \dots &H_{1} \end{bmatrix}$$
0022 | 
0023 | 
0024 | For simplicity, we assume $\beta \leq n^{3}$.
0025 | 
0026 | **The outline of the algorithm to construct generating set:**
0027 | 
0028 |  At $1^{st}$ iteration -
0029 | 
0030 | Step 1. Construct all possible  direct product  $(\pi_1 \times  \pi_2)$ where $\pi_1 \in \beta_1$ and $ \pi_2 \in \beta_2$. 
0031 | 
0032 | There are $| \beta_1 | \times | \beta_2|  <  n^{9}$ direct products (permutations).  All these permutations (direct products) form set $\gamma_1$. Each element of $\gamma_1$ is a permutation that acts on graph $H_1 \cup  H_2$.
0033 | 
0034 | Step 2. Construct/find -
0035 | 
0036 | $\alpha_1 =\{ \pi \in \gamma_1 |  (M_{(1,2)}^{\pi}= M_{(1,2)}) \land ( R_{1,2}^{\pi} = S_{1,2}) \land  (H_1^{\pi} = G_1) \land  (H_2^{\pi} = G_2) \}$ 
0037 | 
0038 | $\alpha_1$ is the set of automorphisms of matrix $M_{(1,2)}$.        $|\alpha_1| < n^{9}$.There are two possible cases-
0039 | 
0040 |   Case 1:  If $|\alpha_1| =1$, then  for each $\pi_1 \in \beta_1$,  there is only one permutation
0041 | $\pi_2 \in \beta_2$. So, there could be maximum $n^{2}$ permutations in $\gamma_1$ but only one permutation could be included in $\alpha_1$.
0042 | 
0043 | 
0044 | 
0045 |    
0046 |  Case 2: If $|\alpha_1| >1$,  we would be able to construct a generating set $\mathcal{S}_1$ of an automorphism group of $Aut(M_{(1,2)})$ Note, that if $\exists \pi_a \in Aut(H)$ such that it acts on   vertices of $H_1 \cup H_2$, then  $  \pi_a \in \langle \mathcal{S}_1 \rangle =Aut(M_{(1,2)})$. So, when we construct direct product of  $\mathcal{S}_1$ and another set,   $\pi_a$ can be found in the resulting generating set. See Theorem 7, on page 31 of **[3]**.The theorem showed how to obtain the automorphism group of an arbitrary graph from the intersection of a specific  permutation group with a direct product of symmetric groups. 
0047 | 
0048 | Step 3. Now, we construct the generating set  $\mathcal{S}_1$  from $\alpha_1$. This construction of generating set can be done in polynomial time (see [3], page 40, theorem 9). From  **[4]**, we find that $|\mathcal{S}_1| \leq log(n!)$ . 
0049 |  $\mathcal{S}_1$ is the  generating set  of automorphism of  $H_1 \cup H_2$ .
0050 |  
0051 |    
0052 | Step 4. We start $2^{nd}$ iteration, for $\beta_3, \mathcal{S}_1$ (instead of $\beta_2$), $ M_{(2,3)}$  where $M_{(2,3)} =\left( \begin{array}{ccc} H_3 & R_{2,3} \\ R_{2,3}^{T} & H_2 \\ \end{array} \right) $.  We find $\gamma_2, \alpha_2$ repeating  steps $1,2$ and construct $\mathcal{S}_2$ (repeating  step $3$)  which  is the  generating set  of automorphism of  graph $H_1 \cup H_2 \cup H_3$. Note that,                    $|\mathcal{S}_2|  \leq log(n!)$ .
0053 | 
0054 | 
0055 | 
0056 | Step  5. We keep repeating above  four   processes, until we find the set $\mathcal{S}_{(x-1)} $  which  is the  generating set  of automorphism of graph $H_1 \cup H_2 \cup H_3 \dots \cup H_x=H $. Note that, $|\mathcal{S}_{(x-1)}|\leq  log(n!)$, since $ \langle \mathcal{S}_{(x-1)} \rangle= Aut(H) \leq S_n$. 
0057 | 
0058 | **Detecting Isomorphism:**  We repeat the process of construction of $\mathcal{S}_{(x-1)}$ for graph $G$ and obtain set $\mathcal{R}_{(x-1)}$. **I assumed, that  the *oracle* that gave $\beta_k$, would provide permutation sets for $G$ also.**
0059 | 
0060 | 
0061 |  Once we generate  generating sets of $G, H$, we can decide isomorphism betwen them [1].
